defect.evidence_quote: In-court identifications require a [[United States v. Wade]] hearing to determine whether they rest on an independent source untainted by the illegal lineup.
defect.locator_note: ^rule-lineup-counsel; disclosed Wade pin-237 supports critical-stage status, Wade pin-242 supports an independent-source hearing, and Gilbert pin-273 supports automatic exclusion plus independent-source hearing, but none states the prosecution-burden allocation.
defect.problem: The core black-letter components are mostly supported, but the statement that an in-court identification survives only if the prosecution shows an independent source is not fully verified by the disclosed cited pinpoints. The disclosed Gilbert/Wade pinpoints establish an independent-source hearing, but do not state the prosecution-burden allocation; no text/*.txt file supplies the missing holding language.
defect.proposed_fix: Either add a verified Wade pinpoint/full opinion text supporting the prosecution-burden clause, or soften the rule to say that an in-court identification survives only if a Wade/Gilbert hearing determines that it rests on an independent source.

reasons: Wade pin-237 says a post-indictment lineup is a critical stage at which the accused is entitled to counsel.
Gilbert pin-273 says lineup-identification testimony is subject to automatic exclusion and in-court identifications require a Wade independent-source hearing.
Kirby pin-689 supports the pre-charge limit, and Ash pin-321/scope_note supports the photographic-display limit.
The disclosed record lacks full opinion text and the relevant pinpoints are marked slip-only/mismatch, so the precise burden phrase cannot be verified from the evidence provided.
residual_risks: If verified Wade text at 240-42 contains the burden allocation, this is a disclosed-record support defect rather than a doctrinal falsehood.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use the softer hearing-based formulation unless a verified Wade burden pinpoint is added.
